top_choice_rationale: P003 pairs two distinct achievements that each turn a biological process into a designable chemical reaction: bifunctional degraders (Crews, Deshaies) that recruit an E3 ligase to remove a chosen protein, and base editing (Liu), single-nucleotide chemical conversion without double-strand breaks. Both changed what researchers and clinicians can do, the mechanisms are defined and independently reproduced, and the allocation respects the three-person cap. I accept the weaknesses (no approved PROTAC drug, base editing close to the 2020 CRISPR prize), but no alternative is clearly better; if only one degrader-centred part is possible I prefer P005, which adds Ciulli's structure-guided ligand design, over P006, where the cereblon glue arm is a separate mechanism discovery.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my molecular-design and bioengineering background may bias me toward tools that reach the clinic, but I have no tie to Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa, Liu, Balasubramanian, Klenerman, or the condensate candidates.
